strings.guide.config.d: Settings holds the LLM-assisted recognition configuration: choose a model provider, enter the API URL / model / key, and run an online connection test.
strings.guide.fab.title: Walkthrough Guide
strings.guide.help.d: Upload the requirements document → review function points → generate the cost table: this is the main workflow.
strings.guide.help_config.d: Configure LLM-assisted recognition (provider / API URL / key) and the application update source, with an online connection test.
strings.guide.help_doc.d: Read the IFPUG methodology and the calculation algorithms, and replay any page’s walkthrough from here.
strings.guide.help_pert.d: Three-point estimation: enter optimistic / most likely / pessimistic values and get the expected duration and variance automatically.
strings.guide.pert.d: The PERT estimate is organised in three steps — Input, Effort Entry and Result — each with its own step bar.
strings.guide.pert_edit.d: Maintain the per-phase items during Effort Entry; load a previous project here to keep editing it.
strings.guide.pert_gen.d: The Result step outputs the expected effort per phase and lets you download the finished table.
strings.guide.pert_in.d: Enter the three-point values for each requirement: optimistic (O), most likely (M) and pessimistic (P); the system computes the expected duration and variance.
strings.guide.work.d: Drag a requirements document in, or click to choose one (.docx). The local engine parses it and produces the IFPUG candidate function points — step 1 of the IFPUG estimate.
strings.guide.work_result.d: Step 3 “Result and download” summarises effort and cost, and exports the finished cost table (Excel) in one click.
strings.guide.work_review.d: Recognition results land in step 2 “Review function points”, where you can tick or adjust each function point’s type and reuse level, then confirm to run the estimate.
strings.guide.work_upload.d: Drop the requirements file onto the dashed frame here, or click it to open the file picker.
strings.help.body.a1: For a single function point: UFP = type weight × complexity weight
strings.help.body.a2f: US = UFP × Reuse Factor × Modification Factor
strings.help.body.a3f: Adjusted FP = ΣUS × Size Changing Factor
strings.help.body.a5f: Cost = Effort (person-days) ÷ 22 × Cost per Person-Month (10k CNY)
strings.help.body.a6: The mid-value ±20% forms the lower/upper bound for negotiation-range reference.
strings.help.body.m1b: IFPUG international function point counting standard
strings.help.body.m1c: (Counting Practices Manual); effort and cost are then converted from benchmark data.
strings.help.body.m2.ei: External Input: processing that brings data into the system
strings.help.body.m2.eif: External Interface File: data referenced but maintained outside this system
strings.help.body.m2.eo: External Output: processing that sends data out of the system
strings.help.body.m2.eq: External Inquiry: retrieval-only queries with no business processing
strings.help.body.m2.ilf: Internal Logical File: data files maintained by this system
strings.help.body.m3: Each function point is weighted at one of three complexity levels (Low / Medium / High): ILF (7/10/15), EIF (5/7/10), EI (3/4/6), EO (4/5/7), EQ (3/4/6).
strings.help.body.m4.reuse_t: : high 1/3, medium 2/3, low 1 (reused functions are not counted at full value)
strings.help.body.m4.scf_t: : reduced or amplified within 0.8~1.4 depending on the estimation stage
strings.help.body.p1: PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) suits change/iteration scenarios where requirements are uncertain and function points are hard to count precisely; experts draw on experience to estimate effort directly with three-point values.
strings.help.body.p2.m_t: : the most probable duration under normal conditions (template column E 'Most Likely')
strings.help.body.p2.o_t: : the shortest duration if everything goes smoothly (template column F 'Minimum')
strings.help.body.p2.p_t: : the longest duration including risks (template column G 'Maximum')
strings.help.body.p4a: Expected person-days are aggregated by phase (requirements / design / development / implementation / shared & remote / on-site maintenance)
strings.help.body.p4c_a: Adjustment coefficients (customer 0.06 / quality 0.06 / change 0.05 / schedule 0.06) are added to get the
strings.help.body.p5: Development-phase details are written from row R8 of the output sheet (columns B/C merged; only column D description plus the E/F/G three values); other phases go to their phase rows. Column H expected values are recalculated automatically by template formulas.
strings.help.body.p6a: On the Input step, upload a requirement document (Word/PDF) or paste text, then click 'Upload & Recognize' on the right to start recognition (greyed out until a file is uploaded). The system routes automatically by the
strings.help.body.p6c: switch: when enabled, AI splits functions/work items and gives optimistic / most likely / pessimistic effort for each; when disabled, local offline analysis is used. Tick items to confirm and continue to effort entry.
strings.help.body.p7c: ; during AI estimation its tech stack, structure, dependencies and size are scanned and injected into the prompt as project-level context, making the effort estimate fit the real code.
strings.help.body.p8a: AI splitting and estimation require enabling the LLM in
strings.help.body.p8c: and filling in the API base URL and key
strings.help.body.p8d: When the LLM is unavailable, docx requirements fall back to local recognition (description only; fill in the three values manually)
strings.help.body.p8e: The project context directory is optional; when unset, AI skips that context without affecting the main flow
